I am seventy this year, and I have worked this land since I was a boy. My father taught me, and now my bones know the seasons better than any book. I finished primary school, but sixty years of planting and harvesting in Longwangmiao have taught me what works on my 16.9 mu. My household has three mouths, and we rely on our well for water. I do not chase new fashions; I stick to what is steady.

My winter wheat is already in the field. I sowed it last autumn after rotary tilling the land. I use the improved variety Luyuan 502 — I buy fresh seed every year because it gives me reliable spikes. This spring I will broadcast urea at green-up, and I have already put down my basal compound fertilizer. With the well pump, I will irrigate three times: once when the wheat wakes up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I also keep an eye on rust and aphids, so I spray insecticide twice, herbicide twice, and fungicide once if the weather turns damp. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant my summer maize. There is no time to waste, so I use the no-tillage seeder right into the wheat stubble. The seed is Denghai 605, a hybrid corn that gives me big ears. I apply one bag of compound fertilizer as basal dressing, and because the summer rains help, I only need to irrigate twice. I spray twice for insects and once for weeds. I have pulled 600 kg per mu from this maize before, and I see no reason it should be less this year.
